## Seminar Overview

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Day 1 — Spatial Data

- GIS fundamentals & coordinate systems
- Open biodiversity data sources (GBIF, iNaturalist)
- Programmatic data retrieval (R, Python)
- Cleaning & quality control
- Hands-on lab session
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Day 2 — Biodiversity Patterns

- Alpha, beta, gamma diversity
- Species distribution modeling (SDM)
- Biogeographical regionalization
- Macroecological patterns
- Case study: Mediterranean flora
:::

::::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this seminar, participants will be able to:

1. **Retrieve** occurrence and environmental data from open repositories
2. **Process** spatial datasets using reproducible workflows
3. **Quantify** biodiversity using appropriate metrics
4. **Model** species distributions across geographic gradients
5. **Interpret** biogeographical patterns in an ecological context

::: callout-tip
All code, datasets, and slides will be available in the GitHub repository.
:::

## Prerequisites & Setup

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
**Software stack**

- R (≥ 4.3) + RStudio
- Python (≥ 3.10)
- QGIS (≥ 3.34)
- Git

**Key R packages**

```r
install.packages(c(
  "sf", "terra", "rgbif",
  "CoordinateCleaner", "dismo",
  "vegan", "biomod2", "tidyverse"
))
```
:::
